answer: Each agent identity must be tied to one carrier-verified mobile number. Sign-up sends a code to the phone, the carrier confirms it is active and not virtual, and its hash is locked to that single identity. Each month the agent repeats the code check or its rewards freeze. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake agents must buy 1,000 SIM cards at $3 each, $3,000 total, plus an $800 SIM farm box and 10 minutes of manual setup per card, 167 hours. At the vertex of this cost curve, a gale of fakes collapses, and the zenith is that every identity carries a real price tag.
